title: Gradient Descent
body:
[[Gradient]]

Minimises a [[Loss Function]] by stepping downhill. On squared error over a linear model the
minimum has a closed form and this is the slow route to it; see [[Linear Regression]] and
[[Least Squares]]. Once the model is non-linear the closed form disappears and this becomes the
only option, which is the whole reason it exists.

It is [[Optimization]] from [[CALCULUS 1]] with too many variables to solve directly. With one
variable you set $f'(x) = 0$ and solve; with a million weights there is no closed form, so you
evaluate the derivative and step downhill instead. Same criterion (a minimum has zero
[[Derivative|slope]]), different algorithm. Each step is a [[Linear Approximation]] to the loss
surface trusted only for a short distance, which is what the learning rate is choosing.
